title: Sell Mineral Rights in Bairoil, WY
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Bairoil, WY | Sweetwater County
metaDescription: Bairoil, WY was literally named for the oil field beneath it. If you hold mineral rights here, get a courthouse-grounded read before you take an offer.
heroLead: Bairoil is one of the few Wyoming towns actually named after the oil field it sits on, and that field has been producing, one way or another, for close to a century.
intro: The Bairoil field sits on the eastern edge of the Great Divide Basin, and it's been developed with waterflood and CO2 enhanced-recovery techniques over the decades to keep production going long after primary recovery tapered off. That's unusual longevity, and it means mineral interests here can have a genuinely long royalty history behind them, unlike a lot of speculative acreage elsewhere in the state.

If your family's interest ties back to this field, the first thing I do is pull your actual production and royalty history, because a field with this kind of enhanced-recovery investment behind it prices very differently from raw undeveloped ground.

sections.heading: Why Bairoil has stayed productive
paragraphs: Primary recovery on a field this old thins out fast, but operators have kept Bairoil going with secondary and tertiary recovery methods, water injection followed by CO2 flooding to push more oil toward the wellbore. That kind of sustained capital investment tells you an operator believes there's more to recover, which matters when I'm assessing whether your interest has runway left or is on its way to stripper-well status.
Courthouse records here go back further than in most of the counties I work, since leasing activity started so early in the field's life.

sections.heading: Pricing a mature producing interest
paragraphs: A mature field like Bairoil doesn't get priced the same way as a new horizontal play. Decline curves are gentler by this stage, but so is upside. I look at your trailing royalty statements, the specific unit's enhanced-recovery status, and comparable Sweetwater County trades before giving you a number, hedged to current activity rather than pinned to a flat multiple.

CO2 flooding in particular is capital intensive, and operators don't commit to it unless the reservoir engineering supports years of additional recovery. That's useful context for an owner trying to decide whether to hold or sell, since it suggests the field still has real runway.

faqs.question: Is Bairoil field still actively producing?
faqs.answer: Yes, portions of it continue under enhanced recovery. I'll check the current status of your specific unit.

faqs.question: I have decades of royalty statements. Does that help?
faqs.answer: Significantly. A long production history gives me real data to price against, rather than speculation.

faqs.question: Why would I sell a producing interest instead of keeping the checks?
faqs.answer: Depends on your goals, decline stage, and whether you'd rather have a lump sum now. I'll walk through both sides honestly before you decide.

faqs.question: Does CO2 flooding change how you value my interest?
faqs.answer: Yes, it typically signals the operator expects more recoverable oil, which supports pricing based on continued production rather than a fast-declining tail.
